literal: the posture of gaining both.
idiomatic: the posture of winning both prizes.

literal: If Yu wins he will surely be grateful for our grace in granting passage;
idiomatic: If Yu wins he will owe us for the passage we granted;

literal: if the Yao clan wins we likewise do not lose the name of aiding a neighbor.
idiomatic: if Yao wins we still keep the name of aiding a neighbor.

literal: Even if Yu takes Guanzhong, it hangs far and is hard to hold.
idiomatic: Even if Yu takes Guanzhong, it lies far and he cannot hold it.

literal: He cannot hold it—ultimately it becomes our possession.
idiomatic: He cannot hold it—in the end it becomes ours.

literal: Now without troubling horses and troops, sit and watch success and failure, fight two leopards and reap lasting gain—this is the superior plan.
idiomatic: Without moving horses or troops, sit and watch the contest, let two leopards fight and reap lasting gain—that is the superior plan.

literal: In planning for a state one chooses profit—why heed marriage bonds or repay the favor of one woman?
idiomatic: States choose profit—why heed marriage ties or repay one woman's favor?

literal: Even if the state abandoned lands south of Mount Heng, Yu could not raise Wu-Yue armies to contest Hebei.
idiomatic: Even if we abandoned lands south of Mount Heng, Yu could not raise Wu and Yue armies to fight for Hebei.

literal: " The debaters still said, "If Yu enters Hangu westward his advance and retreat are cut off and he suffers foe before and behind.
idiomatic: Critics still said, "If Yu enters Hangu from the west he is trapped with enemies fore and aft.

literal: If he comes ashore north, Yao's army will surely not leave the Pass to aid us.
idiomatic: If he lands north, Yao's army will not leave the Pass to help us.

literal: Proclaiming march west while intent is north—that is how the momentum runs.
idiomatic: He proclaims a western march while aiming north—that is how the thrust runs.

literal: " The emperor then followed the assembly and sent Changsun Song to resist him.
idiomatic: The emperor followed the assembly and sent Changsun Song to block him.

literal: They fought at Pancheng and were defeated by the Jin general Zhu Chaoshi.
idiomatic: They fought at Pancheng and were beaten by the Jin general Zhu Chaoshi.

literal: The emperor regretted not using Hao's words.
idiomatic: The emperor regretted not taking Hao's counsel.

literal: In the second year the Jin Governor of Qi Commandery, Wang Yi, came over in surrender.
idiomatic: In year two the Jin Governor of Qi Commandery, Wang Yi, surrendered.

literal: He offered a plan, saying Liu Yu was at Luoyang and urging that troops be sent to cut his rear so Yu's army could be taken without battle.
idiomatic: He urged that with Liu Yu at Luoyang, troops should cut his rear so Yu's army could be taken without fighting.

literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor was pleased.
idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

literal: Hao happened to be before him lecturing on texts.
idiomatic: Hao happened to be before him lecturing on the classics.

literal: The emperor asked Hao, "Yu has marched west to attack and has reached Tong Pass—do you think the affair will succeed?
idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao, "Yu has marched west to Tong Pass—will he succeed?

literal: " Hao said, "Yao Xing loved empty fame without real use; his son Hong is ill and the masses have turned away.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Yao Xing cultivated empty fame without substance; his son Hong is sick and men have deserted him.

literal: Strike their peril and ruin with keen troops and brave generals—conquest is certain.
idiomatic: Strike their weakness with keen troops and brave generals—victory is certain.

literal: " The emperor said, "How does Yu's martial ability compare with Murong Chui?
idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How does Yu's martial prowess compare with Murong Chui?

literal: " Hao said, "Chui inherited his father's and grandfather's resources and was noble from birth.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Chui inherited power and was noble from birth.

literal: His kind rallied to him like moths to flame;
idiomatic: His kind flocked to him like moths to flame;

literal: with slight support he could achieve merit.
idiomatic: with slight backing he could win glory.

literal: Liu Yu rose from bitter poverty; without the use of a single soldier he raised his arm and shouted and destroyed Huan Xuan.
idiomatic: Liu Yu rose from deep poverty; without a single soldier's rank he raised his arm, shouted, and destroyed Huan Xuan.

literal: North he seized Murong Chao; south he shattered Lu Xun.
idiomatic: North he took Murong Chao; south he broke Lu Xun.

literal: If Yu pacifies Yao he will usurp his master.
idiomatic: If Yu pacifies Yao he will supplant his lord.

literal: The Qin lands mix Di and Yi; Yu likewise cannot hold them.
idiomatic: Qin mixes Di and Yi peoples; Yu cannot hold it either.

literal: Qin in the end will belong to our state.
idiomatic: Qin will in the end belong to us.

literal: " The emperor said, "Yu has entered the Pass and cannot advance or retreat—if I send elite horse south to strike Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can Yu stand alone?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yu is in the Pass, unable to advance or retreat—if I send elite cavalry south against Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can he stand alone?

literal: " Hao said, "The northwestern foes are not yet destroyed; Your Majesty cannot personally lead the Six Armies.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Foes in the northwest are not yet crushed; Your Majesty cannot lead the Six Armies in person.

literal: Changsun Song has talent for governing the state but not for aggressive advance—he is no match for Liu Yu.
idiomatic: Changsun Song can govern but cannot press an attack—he is no match for Liu Yu.

literal: I say waiting is not late.
idiomatic: I say to wait is not too late.

literal: " The emperor laughed and said, "Your measure is already settled.
idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "Your judgment is already made.

literal: " Hao said, "Your servant has often privately judged men of recent times and dares not withhold it from Your Majesty.
idiomatic: Hao said, "I have often privately weighed men of recent times and dare not withhold it.

literal: Wang Meng in governing the state was Fu Jian's Guan Zhong;
idiomatic: Wang Meng governing the state was Fu Jian's Guan Zhong;

literal: Murong Ke in assisting the young lord, Murong Chui was Murong Jun's Huo Guang;
idiomatic: Murong Ke guiding a young ruler, Murong Chui was Murong Jun's Huo Guang;

literal: Liu Yu in pacifying rebellion was Sima Dezong's Cao Cao.
idiomatic: Liu Yu crushing rebellion was Sima Dezong's Cao Cao.

literal: " The emperor said, "What do you say of the late emperor?
idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What of the late emperor?

literal: " Hao said, "The Grand Ancestor used the plain folk of the desert north, entered the Han lands, changed customs, and transformed the four seas.
idiomatic: Hao said, "The Grand Ancestor took the plain folk of the northern wastes, entered the Han lands, changed customs, and harmonized the realm.

literal: He stands with Fu Xi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun—how could your servant presume to name him?
idiomatic: He stands with Fu Xi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun—I cannot presume to name his rank.

literal: " The emperor said, "What of Juqu?
idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What of Juqu?

literal: " Hao said, "Juqu's house and state were destroyed; he alone clings in exile, fostered by the Yao clan.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Juqu's house and state are gone; he clings alone in exile, kept alive by Yao.

literal: He does not think to build factions and strengthen neighbors or repay the shame of revenge, but instead joins the Rouran and turns his back on Yao's grace.
idiomatic: He does not build alliances or avenge his shame but joins the Rouran and betrays Yao.

literal: A petty upstart without great strategy—fit only for brutality, in the end to be destroyed by others.
idiomatic: A petty upstart without grand strategy—fit only for cruelty, in the end to be destroyed by others.

literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and talked until midnight.
idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and talked until midnight.

literal: He granted Hao ten hu of pale ale and one liang of crystal war-salt, saying, "I taste your words as I taste this salt and wine—therefore I share the flavor with you."
idiomatic: He gave Hao ten hu of pale ale and one liang of crystal war-salt, saying, "I savor your words as this salt and wine—so I share the taste with you."

literal: In the third year a comet came forth at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, passed the Northern Dipper, threaded Ziwei, and violated Tianbang.
idiomatic: In year three a comet appeared at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, crossed the Northern Dipper, threaded Ziwei, and struck Tianbang.

literal: For more than eighty days it reached the Heavenly River and vanished.
idiomatic: For eighty-odd days it reached the Heavenly River and faded.

literal: The emperor again summoned Confucians and technicians and asked, "In which state will the disaster fall?
idiomatic: The emperor again summoned scholars and technicians and asked, "Which state will bear the omen?

literal: I greatly fear it.
idiomatic: I fear it deeply.

literal: " Hao said, "Strange events arise from men; when men harbor no fault, portents do not arise of themselves.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Omens rise from men; when men harbor no fault, portents do not arise of themselves.

literal: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang usurped the throne the comet's coming and going was exactly as today.
idiomatic: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang seized the throne the comet's course matched today's.

literal: Our state has a respected lord and humble ministers; the people have no other wish.
idiomatic: Our state has a revered lord and humble ministers; the people have no other wish.

literal: This is the response to Jin's usurpation about to perish and Liu Yu's seizure of it.
idiomatic: This answers to Jin's usurping house about to fall and Liu Yu's seizure of it.

literal: " None could overturn Hao's words; the emperor deeply agreed.
idiomatic: None could refute Hao; the emperor was fully convinced.

literal: In the fifth year Song indeed replaced Jin; the southern garrisons presented Song's amnesty changing the era name.
idiomatic: In year five Song replaced Jin; southern garrisons presented Song's amnesty and new era name.

literal: The emperor was then at the southeastern Chichi Pool shooting birds; hearing it, he sent post-horses to summon Hao and told him, "Years ago you spoke of the comet's verification—it has come true.
idiomatic: The emperor was shooting birds at the southeastern Chichi Pool; hearing the news he summoned Hao by post horse and said, "Years ago your comet reading proved true.

literal: Today I first trust Heaven's way.
idiomatic: Today I first trust Heaven's way.

literal: Earlier, when Hao's father was gravely ill,
idiomatic: Earlier, when Hao's father lay gravely ill,

literal: he cut his nails and clipped his hair and at night in the courtyard prayed upward to the Dipper Pole, begging life for his father and asking to die in his stead.
idiomatic: Hao cut his nails and hair and at night in the courtyard prayed to the Pole Star, begging life for his father and offering his own in exchange.

literal: He knocked his head until blood flowed for more than a year without cease; few in the household knew.
idiomatic: He knocked his head until blood ran for more than a year; few in the household knew.

literal: When his father died he observed mourning in full rite; the age praised him.
idiomatic: When his father died he mourned in full rite; the age praised him.

literal: He inherited the title Duke of Baima.
idiomatic: He inherited the dukedom of Baima.

literal: From court ritual and elegant documents, policy edicts, and army-state records, all passed through Hao.
idiomatic: Court ritual, edicts, policy documents, and military records all passed through Hao.

literal: Hao could deliver elegant discourse but was not skilled at linked prose; he focused on institutions, statutes, and classical learning.
idiomatic: Hao excelled at refined discourse but not at literary composition; he focused on institutions, law, and classical learning.

literal: He composed a Family Sacrificial Code, ordering the five ancestral lines and the rites of seasonal offering, with rules of abundance and restraint that could be admired for principle.
idiomatic: He wrote a Family Sacrificial Code, ordering the five lines of ancestry and seasonal rites with rules of plenty and restraint that stood on principle.

literal: By nature he disliked Zhuangzi and Laozi; after a few tens of lines he would cast them aside, saying, "These are deceiving doctrines, remote from human feeling—they cannot be Laozi's own work.
idiomatic: He disliked Zhuangzi and Laozi; after a few dozen lines he would cast them aside, saying, "These are deceiving doctrines, remote from human feeling—they cannot be Laozi's work.

literal: Old Dan studied ritual and was teacher to Confucius—how could he set words to ruin law and disorder the teaching of the former kings?
idiomatic: Old Dan studied ritual and was Confucius's teacher—how could he write to ruin law and disorder the sages' teaching?

literal: What Yuan Sheng called household goods in a basket—things not to be displayed in the royal court."
idiomatic: What Yuan Sheng called goods kept in a family basket—not to be aired in the royal court."

literal: The emperor constantly had slight illness while strange events repeatedly appeared; he sent a palace favorite to ask Hao in secret, "This year the sun is eclipsed in the Stomach and Pleiades, wholly darkening the territories of Zhao and Dai.
idiomatic: The emperor often fell ill while omens multiplied; he secretly asked Hao, "This year the sun eclipses the Stomach and Pleiades, darkening the territories of Zhao and Dai.

literal: My illness has lasted years; I fear sudden collapse—the sons are all young; devise a plan for afterward for me.
idiomatic: My illness has lasted years; I fear sudden death—all my sons are young; plan for what follows.

literal: " Hao said, "Your Majesty's years are still full and the sacred enterprise is unfolding; virtue removes disaster—may you recover in peace.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Your years are still full and your sacred work is rising; virtue dispels disaster—you will recover in peace.

literal: In old times Song Jing saw disaster and cultivated virtue, and Mars withdrew its lodging.
idiomatic: Song Jing once met omens with virtue and Mars withdrew.

literal: I wish Your Majesty to put aside anxious thoughts, calm the spirit and preserve harmony, and not let obscure doctrines harm your sacred mind.
idiomatic: Put aside anxious thoughts, calm your spirit, and do not let obscure doctrines harm your mind.

literal: If it must be, I offer blind words.
idiomatic: If you must have counsel, I offer blind words.

literal: Since the sacred transformation rose like a dragon, the heir apparent has not been honored—thus at the beginning of Yongxing the altars nearly fell.
idiomatic: Since the sacred rise, the heir has not been firmly established—at the opening of Yongxing the altars nearly fell.

literal: Now the Eastern Palace should be built early; choose among the dukes and ministers loyal and worthy whom Your Majesty has long trusted to be tutors;
idiomatic: Build the Eastern Palace early; choose loyal ministers you have long trusted as tutors;

literal: choose trusted ministers close to Your Majesty's heart to fill the posts of guests and companions.
idiomatic: choose trusted men close to your heart as companions.

literal: Entering, grasp the myriad engines; going out, command military affairs; oversee the state and comfort the armies—the six handles in hand.
idiomatic: Let him govern within, command armies without, oversee the realm and comfort the hosts—six handles in his grasp.

literal: Then Your Majesty may roam free without labor, nurturing spirit and prolonging life.
idiomatic: Then Your Majesty may roam at ease, nurturing spirit and prolonging life.

literal: This is the eternal statute of ten thousand generations and the great safeguard against calamity.
idiomatic: That is the eternal statute and the great safeguard against calamity.

literal: The eldest imperial son, taboo name Tao, is nearing twelve, bright, gentle, and the hope of all hearts—if he is installed as heir, the realm will be fortunate.
idiomatic: The eldest son Tao is nearing twelve, bright and gentle, the hope of all—install him as heir and the realm is blessed.

literal: To establish the eldest son is the great canon of ritual; if all must be grown before choosing, reversing the natural order brings the calamity of treading on thin ice over deep water.
idiomatic: The eldest son is ritual's great canon; wait until all are grown and you reverse heaven's order and invite the calamity of thin ice.

literal: From antiquity in the records, rise, fall, survival, and ruin—few are without this cause.
idiomatic: From antiquity in the records, few rises and falls lack this cause.

literal: " The emperor accepted it; he then had Hao present the edict at the ancestral temple, made Taiwu national deputy, and had him preside at the main hall in court.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Hao presented the edict at the ancestral temple, made Taiwu national deputy to preside in the main hall.

literal: Minister of Works Changsun Song, Duke of Gaoyang Xi Jin, and Duke of Beixin An Tong were left assistants, seated in the east wing facing west.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Song, Duke Xi Jin of Gaoyang, and Duke An Tong of Beixin were left assistants in the east wing, facing west.

literal: Hao with Grand Marshal Mu Guan and Palace Attendant Qiu Dui were right assistants, seated in the west wing facing east.
idiomatic: Hao with Grand Marshal Mu Guan and Palace Attendant Qiu Dui were right assistants in the west wing, facing east.

literal: The hundred offices were wholly subject to their hearing.
idiomatic: The hundred offices reported wholly to them.

literal: Mingyuan dwelt in the Western Palace and sometimes hid to watch, listening to their decisions.
idiomatic: Mingyuan stayed in the Western Palace and sometimes watched in secret, listening to their judgments.

literal: Greatly pleased, he told the attendants at his side, "Changsun Song is an old minister of long virtue, serving four reigns, merit preserved in the altars;
idiomatic: Greatly pleased, he told his attendants, "Changsun Song is an old minister of four reigns whose merit preserved the altars;

literal: Xi Jin is quick-witted in debate and famed far and near;
idiomatic: Xi Jin is quick in debate and famed far and wide;

literal: An Tong understands popular feeling and is clear in drill and training;
idiomatic: An Tong understands the people and excels at drill;

literal: Mu Guan grasps the essentials of government and knows my intent;
idiomatic: Mu Guan grasps government and knows my mind;

literal: Cui Hao is broadly learned with strong memory, skilled in the meeting of Heaven and man;
idiomatic: Cui Hao is learned with prodigious memory, skilled in Heaven and man;

literal: Qiu Dui though without great use is scrupulous in public duty.
idiomatic: Qiu Dui lacks grand talent but is scrupulous in office.

literal: With these six to assist my son, it is enough to govern the state.
idiomatic: These six can govern the state for my son.

literal: I with you shall roam the four borders, chastising rebels and soothing submission—we may fulfill our will under heaven.
idiomatic: I with you will roam the four borders, crushing rebels and soothing the submitted—we may fulfill our will under heaven.

literal: " The ministers at the time presented doubtful matters for decision.
idiomatic: The ministers then brought doubtful matters for their decision.
